subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval — post-call next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lawson <tom.lawson@paygrid.com>; Eva Martinez <eva@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid discovery — model fit recap + next steps

Hi Tom / Eva —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of need
- Primary use case: invoice parsing + follow-up generation in a customer support flow (short form generation, slot-filling, and lightweight reasoning).
- Key success metrics: 95%+ slot extraction F1 on priority fields (invoice_no, amount, due_date); generation quality such that human reviewers accept suggested replies >= 90% of the time.
- Constraints: P95 latency <200ms for single-request use cases; sensitive PII handling and audit logging required.

Initial model recommendations (for eval)
- Redwood-Open-7B-8k (quantized 4-bit): good balance of latency and quality for short-form generation.
- Llama-2-13B-8k (7B/13B variants): baseline open models to test parity vs your current proprietary model.
- For high-quality parity targets: evaluate a tuned 13B LLM first, then consider moving to a 30B if quality gaps persist.

Evaluation plan + acceptance thresholds
1) Redwood will run a controlled eval on a representative prompt set (we recommend 1,000 prompts; you can start with 200 samples for a quick sanity check).
2) Metrics: slot extraction (precision/recall/F1), generation accept-rate (human reviewer pass rate), hallucination rate (explicit false facts per 1k tokens).
3) Parity threshold: our proposal is "parity" = within 5 percentage points of your current proprietary baseline on F1 and human accept-rate. If you prefer a tighter threshold (e.g., 3pp), flag that and we’ll adjust the scope.

Data & privacy
- For the eval we can use de-identified CSVs or a secure S3 share. We’ll run the eval in a private environment and provide logs per request (no customer PII stored beyond the evaluation run unless you request).

Next steps (proposed)
- You: share a 200–1,000 sample prompt set (CSV). Attached is a template: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv and a quick sample (paygrid_sample_200.csv).
- Us: we run the eval across the 3 recommended model variants and share a results workbook + sample outputs (model_eval_results_template.xlsx) within 7–10 business days for the 200-sample run; 10–14 business days for 1k.
- Quick follow-up call to review results and discuss canary/production path.

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.csv (template), paygrid_sample_200.csv (example), model_eval_results_template.xlsx (results template)

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the eval run and loop Dev for infra requirements.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Lawson <tom.lawson@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid discovery — model fit recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — really clear. Two quick clarifications before we hand over data: 

1) Parity: when you say within 5 percentage points of our baseline, is that an average across all priority fields or per-field? For us per-field minimums matter (we can’t have invoice_no F1 drop below 90%).
2) Can Redwood run the eval in a locked/private environment where artifacts are removed after the run? We need auditability but also short retention.

Also, are there specific prompt templates you recommend for generation acceptance scoring? We want to ensure our human reviewers see consistent outputs for A/B.

Best,
Tom
Tom Lawson
Head of Product, PayGrid
T: +1 (212) 555-0199

Looping in Dev + Rachel for the eval ops and CS coordination. A few implementation notes and commercial options: 

- Parity: we should ask Tom for per-field minimums. For the deck, propose default per-field floor = baseline - 5pp, but flag invoice_no as "must be >= 90%" if they require.
- Eval environment: Redwood can run in a private VPC project (customer-managed S3 or transient storage). Retention policy: we can set to delete artifacts after 30 days; for shorter retention we can do 7 days if legal signs off.
- Commercial: quick 200-sample sanity eval is complimentary; full 1k eval we charge a small evaluation fee to cover reserved capacity (estimate $3k–$7k depending on model sizes and run time). If PayGrid signs an MQA/commit this fee can be credited.

Dev — can you confirm required inputs (S3 link vs. CSV upload) and an infra ETA for a 200-sample job? Rachel — FYI on CS reviewer workflow and labeling for accept-rate.

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid discovery — model fit recap + next steps

Tom — thanks for the questions. Short answers below, plus links and requested items.

1) Parity per-field vs aggregate
- We can evaluate both. Per-field minimums are easy to report in the results sheet; our default parity proposal was aggregate, but we will respect per-field constraints you set. Please mark any field-level "must be" thresholds in the CSV.

2) Eval environment & retention
- We will run the evaluation in a dedicated private run: ephemeral S3 bucket (or your S3) + isolated compute. Artifacts will be removed after the agreed retention window. If you need 7-day retention, we can push that through but legal will need to sign a short addendum.

3) Prompt templates for acceptance scoring
- Attached is a short doc inside the results template that defines reviewer instructions and a 3-point rubric (Accept / Edit / Reject) for generation outputs. Consistent reviewer instructions + 3 reviewers per sample gives robust accept-rate estimates.

4) Links & sandbox
- Colab evaluation harness (read-only): https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1PayGridEval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/PG-2025-037

Next steps
- If you can upload the 200-sample CSV to this thread or point us to an S3 share, we’ll queue the sanity run.
- We’ll include Llama-2-13B and Redwood-Open-7B runs by default. If you want to add a tuned 13B, note that in your reply.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the 30–45 minute results review 1–2 business days after the run completes.

Regards,
Marissa
